newsitem.title: USA: NHL-STARS BEAT ISLES TO CLINCH CENTRAL DIVISION TITLE.
newsitem.headline: NHL-STARS BEAT ISLES TO CLINCH CENTRAL DIVISION TITLE.

text.p: Benoit Hogue scored with 33 seconds left to give the Stars to a 5-4 victory over the the New York Islanders as Dallas clinched the Central Division title and reached the 100-point plateau on Wednesday.

Jere Lehtinen, Mike Modano, Bill Huard and Bob Bassen also scored for the surprising Stars, who extended their winning streak to seven games and moved within three points of Colorado in the battle for the best record in the league and the top Western Conference playoff berth.
"Division champion has a nice ring to it," said Modano. "Who knows, we could catch Colorado, that's what we want."
The Stars have not won a division crown since 1984 when they were the Minnesota North Stars.
Dave McLlwain's powerplay goal with 6:24 left in the third lifted New York into a 4-4 tie, but Hogue, a former Islander, scored his 18th goal for the game-winner.
Pat Verbeek tapped the puck away from Todd Bertuzzi and Hogue beat goaltender Tommy Salo with a rising wrist shot from the right faceoff circle.
"This goal is my biggest," said Hogue. "Clinching the division after not making the playoffs (last year) is terrific."
Dallas, which finished last in the Central last season, is unbeaten in 11 games (9-0-2).

"I'm not so much excited that we clinched the division tonight as that we were able to pick up 100 points," Dallas coach Ken Hitchcock said. "One hundred points is a sign of a good, consistent hockey club that comes to play every night."
In Calgary, Peter Forsberg recorded his first hat trick of the season and Craig Billington made 23 saves as the Colorado Avalanche beat the Flames 5-1 to stay three points ahead of the surging Stars.

Forsberg gave Colorado a 1-0 lead with 4:23 left in the first period. The slick Swede got his second goal 90 seconds into the second to make it 3-0 and completed the hat trick and the scoring with his 26th goal of the season with 27 seconds left in the middle period.
The red-hot Forsberg has points in 14 of his last 15 games with 13 goals and 13 assists.
Adam Deadmarsh and Rene Corbet also tallied for Colorado. Marty McInnis spoiled Billington's shutout bid at 4:34 of the second period.
In Buffalo, Ron Tugnutt posted his first shutout in more than three years as the Ottawa Senators blanked the Sabres 2-0 to move into the final Eastern Conference playoff spot.
Shaun Van Allen and Bruce Gardiner scored for the Senators, who who have won three in a row and moved ahead of Washington and Hartford into eighth place in the East.
Tugnutt needed to make just 15 saves, as Buffalo managed five shots in the first period and only three in the third.
Ottawa got off 36 shots on goal with Dominik Hasek making 34 saves for the Sabres, whose winless streak reached six games (0-5-1).
In Hartford, Stephane Quintal and Mark Recchi scored 53 seconds apart late in the first period and Jocelyn Thibault made 24 saves as the Montreal Canadiens beat the Whalers 4-1.
Recchi and Saku Koivu each had a goal and an assist for the Canadiens, who improved to 5-2-3 in their last 10 games and solidified their hold on seventh place in the East.
Keith Primeau had the only goal for Hartford, a short-handed tally with 3:56 to go in the first period that staked the Whalers to a 1-0 lead.
Quintal tied the game 80 seconds later with the first of Montreal's four unanswered goals.
In Toronto, Felix Potvin stopped 33 shots and Wendel Clark and Sergei Berezin scored first-period goals as the Maple Leafs beat the struggling Florida Panthers 3-1.
Tie Domi added a powerplay goal and Steve Sullivan had two assists for Toronto.
Dave Lowry scored the lone goal for Florida, which is winless in its last four games (0-3-1).
The Panthers already clinched a playoff berth but stand just four points ahead of the fifth-place New York Rangers in the East with home ice advantage in the first round at stake.
In San Jose, Marty McSorley scored with just 22 seconds left in regulation to lift the Sharks to a 5-5 tie with the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim.
McSorley's wrist shot from the left faceoff circle caromed off the back of Anaheim defenceman Dmitri Mironov and trickled past goaltender Guy Hebert.
Jeff Friesen had two goals and two assists for the Sharks, who took a 3-1 lead into the third period.
Paul Kariya and Teemu Selanne, who notched his 48th goal, each had a goal and two assists for Anaheim, which moved one point ahead of fifth-place Phoenix in the Western Conference.
